scope: canonical rendered Metkagram learning surfaces after Pattern/Frame/Move/Contrast/Choice/Route/Bridge semantics are complete

findings.evidence: Continuation candidates are accepted only when both source and destination are canonical, indexable URLs present in the completed sitemap.
Continuation cards name the destination page and its learner-facing surface such as Pattern Atlas, Pattern Practice, Pattern Lens, Pattern Contrast or Pattern Choice.
The postprocessor derives continuation only from anchors already present inside the rendered main content, excluding header/footer/global navigation.
No parallel relation graph is invented; existing rendered links produced by Frames, Moves, Contrasts, Choice, Routes and Bridges remain the semantic authority.
Metkagram's shared renderer already owns BreadcrumbList generation and page-specific visible breadcrumbs; this layer does not emit a conflicting breadcrumb hierarchy.
Learning pages with at least two existing contextual links to other canonical learning pages receive a bounded Continue learning block using up to three of those existing routes.
The existing share bar already provides native/share-network/copy/print actions; this layer extends it with browser-local Save and canonical Cite rather than adding a second utility bar.
Cite copies Metkagram, the visible page title and canonical URL without inventing authorship, DOI, learning efficacy or licensing permission.
No Preferred Sources control is added until source-preference availability and publisher applicability are independently verified.

The read-only Audit stage verifies canonical continuation sources/targets, noindex boundaries, Save/Cite extension and exact rendered manifest; production smoke verifies the deployed manifest and a bounded live sample.
